source.title: Generalizability of Neural Networks Minimizing Empirical Risk Based on Expressive Ability
source.authors: Li-Jia Yu; Yi-Bo Miao; Yifan Zhu; Xiao-Shan Gao; Li-Jun Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cut-off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical results on empirical-risk minimizers and reports width and training-set-size experiments, using accuracy plots to examine generalization.
record.gate_note: Appendix L reports MNIST accuracy experiments relevant to width and data size. The paper does not report random-label fitting, optimizer comparisons, batch-size sweeps, dropout, or measured sharpness. The theoretical bounds and examples are not separate experimental outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports improved MNIST test accuracy with width, but never establishes which widths achieve zero training error or measures widening beyond that threshold. Its theoretical accuracy lower bound also does not establish that actual test error decreases monotonically with width. Thus it does not test V2's defining claim, and it tests none of the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive sufficient width and sample-size conditions for high population accuracy of bounded-parameter networks minimizing or approximately minimizing binary cross-entropy, conditional on distribution expressibility. They also establish sample-complexity lower bounds and discuss robustness, insufficient width and loss choice. They describe the MNIST experiments as consistent with their theory. Neither the theory nor these experiments establishes monotonically decreasing actual test error beyond interpolation.
record.recipe_differences: The principal results concern theoretical empirical-risk minimizers, not the original studies' standard-training memorization experiments. Appendix L uses two-layer ReLU networks, gradient descent, and weight clipping after each step.
record.method_sensitivity: Appendix L reports that accuracy changes with network width and training-set size; width gains are limited at fixed data size, and data gains are limited for small networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix L reports that wider weight-clipped two-layer ReLU networks improve MNIST test accuracy, with diminishing gains at fixed training-set size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width can improve held-out accuracy without establishing whether the networks are beyond the interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix L reports accuracy improvements with more training data, limited for smaller networks; width 200 with all data approximately matches width 400 with 40% of the data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Network width and training-set size jointly constrain classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.4 and 4.8 give population-accuracy lower bounds for bounded-parameter empirical-risk minimizers under expressibility assumptions; increasing width improves the bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficient network width and sample size can guarantee high population accuracy under the stated assumptions.

record.problems: The experimental accuracy values are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. Training error, convergence, seeds, and uncertainty are not stated. The experiments use weight clipping, so they do not establish the stated no-explicit-regularization condition.
record.rows_left_out: No additional experimental result rows identified. Appendix L Figures 1 and 2 are included as figure-only rows because the text gives qualitative descriptions but no exact values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training under the same architecture and recipe.
Whether test error continues decreasing when width increases beyond an established zero-training-error threshold under converged training without explicit regularization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and dependence on tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover accuracy.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, dropout strength and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text omits readable figure values, so the experimental findings can be assessed only from the authors' qualitative descriptions. No additional result directly testing a listed version was identified.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment fits random labels or compares their held-out accuracy with natural-label accuracy.

The experiments do not state that training reaches zero error or convergence, and use weight clipping after each gradient-descent step. No downsampled CIFAR-10 results or explicit training-error measurements are reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

rows.subject: two-layer networks with ReLU activation function
rows.operation_detail: Train networks at different widths and measure test-set accuracy; parameters are weight-clipped after each gradient-descent step.
rows.note: The authors state that increasing network size improves accuracy, with a limitation on that improvement when data size is fixed. Exact plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: The reported width trend is valid, but training error, interpolation threshold and convergence are unreported, and training uses weight clipping. It cannot establish generalization improvements beyond the width needed to fit. Diminishing accuracy gains alone do not warrant a partial state or limits_scope verdict for V2.

rows.subject: two-layer networks with ReLU activation function
rows.operation_detail: Train on increasing fractions of the original training set and measure accuracy.
rows.measure: accuracy; text does not specify test-set accuracy for Figure 2
rows.note: The authors state that increasing data helps, with limited improvement for small networks; they compare 200-width on all data with 400-width on 40% of the data. Exact plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: The main manipulation is training-set size, which no version claims improves accuracy. Comparisons across widths also lack an identified interpolation threshold; Figure 2's accuracy split is unspecified. Limited benefits from adding data to small networks do not qualify V2.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MNIST width sweep with weight clipping
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy improves with width, but the authors describe the gain as limited when data size is fixed; training error and convergence are not reported (R1). The data-size experiments also report limited gains for small networks (R2).
